outputs.L1: An apparatus comprises a memory and a controller. The memory is configured to store data and may comprise a write buffer and a plurality of memory dies. Each memory die may have a size smaller than a total size of the memory and may include a plurality of cells. The memory may perform a program operation to write to and verify one or more of the plurality of cells in response to receiving a program command. The controller may be configured to issue the program command to program the plurality of memory dies and to issue a polling status command after issuing the program command to obtain a number of the cells that failed verification during the program operation. outputs.L2: A device includes a memory and a controller. The memory is arranged to store information and may include a write buffer along with multiple memory dies. Each memory die may be smaller than the overall capacity of the memory and may contain multiple cells. When a program command is received, the memory may carry out a programming process that writes data to, and verifies, one or more of the cells. The controller may be arranged to send the program command for programming the memory dies and, after sending that command, to send a polling status command to determine how many cells failed verification during the programming process. Upon receiving the polling status command from the controller, the memory provides a count of the bit-lines in the write buffer that are not in an inhibited state.
outputs.L3:
The apparatus includes a memory and a controller configured to manage operations of the memory. The memory is configured to store data and may include, for example, a write buffer and a plurality of memory dies. The write buffer may temporarily hold data to be written, while the memory dies provide the storage area in which the data is ultimately programmed.

Each memory die has a storage capacity that is smaller than the total storage capacity of the memory as a whole. In other words, the overall memory capacity may be distributed across multiple memory dies. Each memory die includes a plurality of memory cells, and the memory cells may be arranged along bit-lines and word-lines to enable programming, reading, and verification operations.

In response to receiving a program command, the memory performs a program operation. During the program operation, data is written to selected memory cells. The memory also performs a verification process to determine whether the selected memory cells have been successfully programmed to their intended states. If one or more cells do not satisfy the required verification criteria, those cells may be identified as having failed verification.

The controller is configured to issue a polling status command to the memory in connection with the program operation. In response to the polling status command, the controller obtains status information from the memory, including a count associated with verification failures. The count may indicate a number of memory cells that failed verification during the program operation, or a number of bit-lines associated with cells that failed verification. This information may be used by the controller to monitor the progress or quality of the program operation and to determine whether further action is required.
outputs.L4:
An apparatus includes a controller coupled to a memory device having a memory array and associated memory circuitry. The memory device includes a plurality of memory dies and a memory configured to store data for programming operations, including a write buffer that holds data to be written to selected memory cells. During a program operation, the controller provides program data to the memory device, and the memory device applies one or more program pulses to selected memory cells in the plurality of memory dies. After a program pulse, the memory device performs a verification operation to determine whether the selected memory cells have reached their intended programmed states.

To monitor the progress and result of the programming operation, the controller issues a polling status command to the memory device. In response to the polling status command, the memory device evaluates the state of bit-lines associated with the write buffer. In particular, the memory device determines a count of bit-lines that are not in an inhibited state. A bit-line in an inhibited state may correspond to a memory cell that has successfully passed verification or no longer requires additional programming, while a bit-line that is not in an inhibited state may correspond to a memory cell that has not yet passed verification and remains subject to further programming.

The memory device reports the count of bit-lines not in the inhibited state to the controller as status information. Based on this reported count, the controller can determine whether one or more memory cells have failed verification during the program operation. The controller may use the count to assess the severity or extent of the verification failure, determine whether additional programming pulses should be applied, identify problematic portions of the memory array, or take corrective action such as retrying the program operation, marking a region as defective, adjusting programming parameters, or invoking error management procedures.

By providing the controller with a count of bit-lines that remain uninhibited, rather than merely providing a pass or fail indication, the apparatus enables more detailed monitoring of programming performance across multiple memory dies. This allows the controller to identify cells that failed verification during programming more efficiently and to manage program operations with improved accuracy and reliability.

The word **“the”** points to something specific, while **“each”** reminds us to notice every individual part. Together, they help us think about both the whole and the details.

In life, we often focus on **the** big picture: the goal, the plan, the final result. However, **each** small step matters just as much. Each choice, each effort, and each moment contributes to what we eventually become. The journey is not made by one great action alone, but by many small actions repeated with care.

Whether in learning, work, or relationships, the same idea applies. The success we want depends on each lesson we study, each task we complete, and each person we treat with respect. By valuing each part, we strengthen the whole.

In the end, **the** important thing is to remember that **each** detail has meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a memory device apparatus where a controller issues program and polling status commands, and the memory reports a count of failed verified cells based on bit-lines not in an inhibited state in a write buffer.
counterfactuals.output: A memory device apparatus includes a memory array having a plurality of memory cells coupled to bit-lines, a write buffer configured to store inhibit information for the bit-lines during a program operation, and control circuitry coupled to the memory array and the write buffer. A controller is configured to issue a program command to the memory device and to issue a polling status command during or after execution of the program command. In response to the polling status command, the control circuitry determines a count of failed verified memory cells based on bit-lines identified in the write buffer as being in a non-inhibited state, the non-inhibited state corresponding to memory cells that have not satisfied a program verify condition. The memory device reports the count to the controller as status information associated with the program operation. The reported count may be used by the controller to determine program completion, program failure, or further program control for the memory array.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise patent disclosure paragraph about NAND flash programming in which a polling status command returns the number of bit-lines in a write buffer that are not inhibited.
counterfactuals.output: In one embodiment, a NAND flash memory device includes a write buffer coupled to a plurality of bit-lines and control logic configured to perform a program operation on selected memory cells. During or between programming pulses, the control logic determines, for the write buffer, a count of bit-lines that are not inhibited from programming, such as bit-lines corresponding to data states that still require threshold-voltage advancement. In response to receipt of a polling status command from a controller, the memory device returns status information including the count of non-inhibited bit-lines in the write buffer. The controller may use the returned count to monitor programming progress, estimate remaining program time or current demand, adjust scheduling of subsequent operations, or determine whether additional program pulses are likely to be required, without transferring the contents of the write buffer.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, a memory system including a controller, write buffer, plurality of memory dies, program command, verification of cells, and reporting of failed bit-line counts.
counterfactuals.output:
A memory system is provided comprising a memory controller, a write buffer operatively coupled to the memory controller, and a plurality of non-volatile memory dies each including a memory cell array having a plurality of memory cells arranged along word lines and bit lines. The memory controller is configured to receive host write data, temporarily store the host write data in the write buffer, and issue, to at least one selected memory die of the plurality of memory dies, a program command for programming data corresponding to the host write data into selected memory cells of the selected memory die.

In response to the program command, the selected memory die is configured to perform a program operation on the selected memory cells and to perform a verification operation to determine whether the selected memory cells have reached one or more target program states. The verification operation may include sensing threshold voltage states of the selected memory cells and identifying, for respective bit lines coupled to the selected memory cells, whether one or more memory cells associated with the respective bit lines fail to satisfy a program verification criterion.

The selected memory die is further configured to generate failure information indicative of a number of failed bit lines detected during the verification operation. The failure information may include, for example, a failed bit-line count representing a total number of bit lines associated with cells that failed verification, or a plurality of failed bit-line counts respectively corresponding to different program states, word lines, pages, memory planes, or program-verify cycles.

The selected memory die is configured to report the failed bit-line count to the memory controller, either together with or separate from a program status indication. The memory controller is configured to receive the reported failed bit-line count and determine, based at least in part on the reported failed bit-line count, whether the program operation is acceptable, whether an additional program pulse or retry operation is to be performed, whether data stored in the write buffer is to be retained for recovery or reprogramming, or whether the data is to be programmed to a different location in one or more of the plurality of memory dies. In some embodiments, the memory controller compares the failed bit-line count with a predetermined threshold and determines a pass condition when the failed bit-line count is less than or equal to the predetermined threshold, and determines a fail condition when the failed bit-line count exceeds the predetermined threshold.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an AI-generated patent abstract for an apparatus where memory performs program-and-verify operations and reports, in response to a polling status command, a count associated with non-inhibited bit-lines.
counterfactuals.output: An apparatus includes a memory array having a plurality of memory cells coupled to respective bit-lines and control circuitry coupled to the memory array. The control circuitry is configured to perform a program-and-verify operation on selected memory cells, including inhibiting bit-lines associated with memory cells that have satisfied a verify condition and maintaining as non-inhibited bit-lines associated with memory cells that have not satisfied the verify condition. The control circuitry is further configured to receive a polling status command during the program-and-verify operation and, in response to the polling status command, output status information including a count associated with the non-inhibited bit-lines. The count may indicate a number of bit-lines or memory cells remaining to be programmed or verified, thereby enabling an external controller to monitor programming progress before completion of the program-and-verify operation.
